summary: Market sentiment is cautiously risk-off, with geopolitical tension in the Middle East dominating investor attention as stalled US-Iran nuclear talks, new US sanctions grounding Iranian flights, and Houthi missile activity in Yemen collectively push oil prices higher, weighing on equities particularly in the UK. On the macro front, Federal Reserve officials are signaling continued monetary tightening, with New York Fed's Williams calling another rate hike by year-end "reasonable" and Philadelphia Fed's Paulson flagging only "modest" moves ahead, reinforcing a higher-for-longer rate environment that is pressuring bonds and driving a boom in bond-alternative trades on Wall Street. In individual stocks, Meta is approaching a new 52-week high on bullish sentiment around its AI strategy following the Muse rollout, while MGM Resorts tumbled 9% after Barry Diller's IAC rescinded its takeover bid, and pet retail names are catching a bid on stronger-than-expected consumer spending in the category. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include an escalation of the Iran-Hormuz situation that could spike crude prices further, persistent inflation keeping the Fed hawkish, and growing legal pressure on prediction markets following New York's lawsuit against Polymarket shortly after its action against Kalshi. In the near term, the market faces a binary geopolitical catalyst around US-Iran negotiations — a phased deal reopening Hormuz would be broadly risk-positive, while a breakdown could send oil sharply higher and tighten financial conditions further, keeping equities volatile through the week.
